svg.text: Northwind Governance Control Plane: architecture at a glance
Capstone Part D | Policy inheritance, team-boundary RBAC, and the two gaps Part D closes from Part C
Northwind (Intermediate Root)
3 policies assigned here: tags, regions, diagnostics
inherits automatically
Platform subscriptions
Identity, Management, Connectivity - all three inherit
Corp -> future AVD subscriptions
Will inherit the same 3 policies automatically, Part E
Enforced by ARM at creation time - a Deny policy blocks a violating
resource before it exists, not by convention someone could skip.
RBAC TEAM BOUNDARIES - least privilege, not one broad role (platform/rbac)
Platform Engineer
Northwind MG - PIM-eligible
Identity Administrator
sub-northwind-identity only - PIM-eligible
Network Administrator
sub-northwind-connectivity only
Security Reader
Tenant root, read-only - STANDING
Security Administrator
Policy exemptions only - PIM-eligible
AVD / Ops (future)
Not defined yet - Part E/F's job
CORRECTED: all six roles above are built in platform/rbac/, not platform/security/ -
moved here during the PIM remediation pass (see the implementation tracker).
GAPS PART D CLOSES FROM PART C'S BUILD (platform/security)
Key Vault (kv-northwind-platform)
DC admin credentials + Connect Sync service
account now live here - RBAC-authorized, Private Endpoint only
Azure Bastion Premium x2
Session recording (Premium-only, per Microsoft
Learn) for privileged access to Part C's domain controllers
BREAK-GLASS - the one control this design does not fully close
2 cloud-only Global Admin accounts, standing (not PIM), excluded from Conditional Access
Credentials must be split OFFLINE, not just stored in the Key Vault above
HOW TO READ THIS IN 60 SECONDS
1 Policy inheritance is automatic and ARM-enforced - Part E's future AVD subscriptions get all 3 Part B policies with zero new policy work required.
2 RBAC is split by team, not one broad Platform role - Identity and Network administrators have no reason to touch each other's infrastructure.
3 A genuine, disclosed tension: break-glass credentials living in Key Vault depend on the same Entra ID that might be degraded when break-glass is actually needed.
4 Workload/AVD security (session host baselines, watermarking) is deliberately NOT here - Part F's job, once host pools exist to apply a baseline to.
5 All RBAC/PIM roles shown above live in platform/rbac/ - not platform/security/, where they were first (incorrectly) built. Corrected during the PIM remediation, and again here in the diagram.

Original architecture diagram for this capstone, not Microsoft's. Verified against terraform/capstone-northwind/platform/security (Key Vault, Bastion, break-glass) and platform/rbac (all RBAC/PIM roles) and Part D, August 2026. Self-contained, no remote icon dependency.
